_about: Names for Karateka's routines and globals, with the evidence for each.
This file exists because `recovered/karateka.asm` is gitignored and must
stay so -- a byte-identical reconstruction is the game. What can be kept
is the *reading*: addresses, names, and why. Run tools/annotate.py to
apply these to a freshly generated listing and get source that still
reassembles to the original, byte for byte.
Addresses are image offsets. Add 0x200 for a file offset. Globals are
offsets from DS, which the entry stub sets to image + 0x6CA0.
`why` is not decoration. A name with no evidence behind it is a guess
that will be believed by the next reader, and this project has already
published three of those and had to withdraw them.

0x0002: the MZ entry from CS:IP; sets DS once and never again
0x0629: rand() * (n+1), high word taken -- uniform 0..n with no divide
0x083C: takes an id, sets both stream pointers from two tables
0x0AE7: one byte per scanline, add di 0x50
0x0B95: run-length decoder, called once per output byte
0x1277: text in, byte code out; called with (name, destination)
0x1364: arm 0 of the compiler's jump table at 0x163E
0x162D: arm 13; emits 0xFF, the only opcode that is not 2*index
0x1976: walks a compiled library recording each block's offset; 42 of them, frames 17 bytes
0x19A2: the same for the library at 0xCE3E
0x19EE: builds n section tables from a scenery script; n is 1 or 6
0x190B: compile a named script and run it
0x1AC2: scene 0..3 -> bal00..bal03 through the pointer table at DS:0x021C
0x1D07: reached from every arm of the pose switch; calls the input layer
0x228B: sparse (pose, arm) dispatch, seventeen cases, table at 0x2247
0x2324: advance or restart the player's move
0x2605: the AI: its pose, the player's pose, the distance
0x2A49: plays the attract sequence; computes a distance a keyboard reader would not want
0x3A2D: sets the walls and the section index
0x3A8A: copies section [0xC3A6] out of the three tables
0x3B19: pose 31, and random(2)*12 for an aggression of 0, 12 or 24
0x3B5C: knock back 4 px and take a point; the scripted kind, not the fight kind
0x4149: called from inside pose_handler at 0x1D2A and 0x1DAA
0x425E: port 0x3BA with a counted loop -- display detection, NOT the joystick
0x4273: 0x55AA written into video memory and read back
0x42D1: port 0x3BF, then the sync wait above
0x43AA: attacker's pose, distance, target's stance -> 4 for a miss, 2 or 3 for a hit
0x44D3: turns the stick bitmask into an intent, given the player's pose
0x4756: buttons plus both axes against the calibration bounds
0x4840: Lattice C: walks FILE slots from 0xE1B0 to 0xE2C8, stride 14

0x010C: written from each frame's first set_pos byte; read by the guard's AI
0x0114: 13 at the start of a fight
0x0118: NOT health: counts down while the player stays beyond 330 px
0x011A: the second stage of the same timer
0x0126: +3 per hit; runs down and gives a point back
0x0130: 1 to 7, advanced by a plain inc
0x0142: per level; adds one to the section index
0x0156: 0 the human plays, 1 the demo does
0x00EC: bit 0 of the frame's second set_pos byte
0x00FC: read by the chooser on the next frame
0xBCD5: inc_x is added here, then clamped to the walls
0xC3A6: 3, 4 or 5 -- which stretch of wall, and so how many opponents
0xC3D2: the current frame; 0xFF at it ends the move
0xD5AE: the frame's second byte >> 1; the hit test's third argument
0xE112: stance -> class 0..9; classes 3 and 4 can never be hit
0xE19F: direction bits and the two buttons
0x0017: Lattice C's; every prologue compares sp against it
